form_analysis.feedback: Excellent aftercare form for laser wart removal with comprehensive guidance on HPV containment and recurrence prevention. Strong emphasis on the extended treatment timeline and monitoring for resolution.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare is for laser removal of warts caused by human papillomavirus (HPV). Laser destroys wart tissue and stimulates immune response. Focus on preventing spread and recurrence.

instructions.general_directive: Follow for 1-2 weeks wound care, with ongoing monitoring for recurrence. Warts often require multiple treatments.

sections.title: Laser Wart Mechanism
sections.content: Pulsed dye laser (PDL) targets blood vessels feeding wart, OR CO₂ laser vaporizes wart tissue. Both stimulate immune response against HPV virus.

sections.title: Immediate Post-Laser Response
items: Darkening/blackening of wart tissue.
Possible blistering around wart.
Pain/tenderness for 24-72 hours.
Crater-like wound after wart tissue separates.

sections.title: HPV Containment Protocol (CRITICAL)
items: Keep treated area covered with bandage for 1 week.
Wash hands after touching area.
Do not share towels, shoes, or personal items.
Wear flip-flops in public showers/pools.
Avoid shaving over area until healed.

sections.title: Recurrence Prevention
items: Warts may recur in same or new locations.
Monitor surrounding skin for new growths.
Consider topical salicylic acid on surrounding skin as prevention.
Boost immune system: Adequate sleep, nutrition, stress management.

sections.title: Pain Management
items: More painful than other laser procedures.
Over-the-counter pain relievers as needed.
Cold compresses for first 48 hours.
Elevate if on foot to reduce throbbing.

sections.title: Monitoring for Resolution
items: Wart tissue sloughs off in 7-14 days.
Skin underneath may be pink/sensitive.
Complete resolution takes 4-6 weeks to assess.
May require 2-4 treatments at 4-6 week intervals.

sections.title: Special Considerations
items: Plantar warts (feet): May require longer healing, pressure offloading.
Periungual warts (around nails): Risk of nail damage.
Immunocompromised patients: Higher recurrence rate.
Multiple warts: May spread during treatment process.
